response.sql: WITH valid AS (SELECT t.tradekind, ab.abhvreg FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref WHERE t.tradekind IS NOT NULL), counts AS (SELECT tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM valid GROUP BY tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM counts), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts), above AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share, s.cnt - st.avg_cnt AS excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN stats st WHERE s.cnt > st.avg_cnt) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS sum_counts, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above

assumptions.assumption: Trader types are the tradekind values that have at least one qualifying analysis record; types with zero records are not included in the average count. The enum defines four types, so this is a judgment call.
Rows with a NULL tradekind are not a trader type and are excluded.

Each advancedbehavior row is one analysis record. Inner joins through transactionrecord (translink to transreg, trdref to tradereg) enforce that both the transaction and the trader exist. Each transaction joins to exactly one trader, so no rows are duplicated.

alternatives.interpretation: Use all four defined trader types (Market Maker, Broker, Individual, Institution), so a type with no qualifying records counts as zero in the average count and in the total.
alternatives.sql: WITH types(tradekind) AS (VALUES ('Market Maker'), ('Broker'), ('Individual'), ('Institution')), valid AS (SELECT t.tradekind, ab.abhvreg FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref), counts AS (SELECT ty.tradekind, COUNT(v.abhvreg) AS cnt FROM types ty LEFT JOIN valid v ON v.tradekind = ty.tradekind GROUP BY ty.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM counts), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts), above AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share, s.cnt - st.avg_cnt AS excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN stats st WHERE s.cnt > st.avg_cnt) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS sum_counts, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a NULL tradekind as its own trader type group, so those analysis records are counted and included in the total and average.
